title: Investigation of organized crime in interstate commerce. Hearings before a Special Committee to Investigate Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, United States Senate, 81st Congress, Part 10
venue: U.S. Senate (Kefauver Committee), via Internet Archive
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Flamingo ownership under Siegel and successors; Lansky stock
quote: Mr. Halley. Did Lansky have some stock ? Mr. Wiener. I think he did.
summary: Sworn Senate testimony (Nov 1950) by the Flamingo's attorney lists the post-Siegel stockholders and says Meyer Lansky held some stock, while Siegel held about 22 percent.
limits: Witness testimony ('I think'), not a committee finding; the witness could not state Lansky's share. Lansky is dead. Hearings predate the Sands (1952) and later venues.

title: Investigation of organized crime in interstate commerce. Hearings before a Special Committee to Investigate Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, United States Senate, 81st Congress, Part 10
venue: U.S. Senate (Kefauver Committee), via Internet Archive
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Desert Inn ownership by the Cleveland group
quote: Three of us, Mr. Kleinman, Mr. Tucker, and myself have 13 percent each, which would be 39 percent.
summary: Dalitz testified under oath that the Cleveland partners held about 39 percent and, with McGinty and C. Jones, about 59 percent of the Desert Inn, with Wilbur Clark holding most of the rest.
limits: Shows disclosed ownership by the Cleveland group, not a hidden interest. Dalitz is dead. Part of his testimony was refused by direction of the chair.

title: Investigation of organized crime in interstate commerce. Hearings before a Special Committee to Investigate Organized Crime in Interstate Commerce, United States Senate, 81st Congress, Part 10

ask_addressed: mob-tie: committee record on Dalitz's Cleveland background

summary: Committee staff summary on Morris (Moe) Dalitz, alias Davis, ties him to the Mayfield Road gang of Cleveland and to associates in Detroit, New York and the Capone gang.
limits: Phrased as an allegation ('it was alleged'); it is a congressional record of association, not a conviction or a Nevada board finding.

title: Mob Ties
ask_addressed: mob-tie: Flamingo funding and Desert Inn rescue by Cleveland group
quote: Moe Dalitz and the Cleveland Mayfield Road Gang bailed out the original builder and owner of the Desert Inn
summary: Sun history says Lansky and Siegel funded the Flamingo's construction and that Dalitz's Cleveland group rescued Wilbur Clark's unfinished Desert Inn; it says Siegel overran the cost sixfold.
limits: Newspaper/popular history; relies on secondary books (Green Felt Jungle, Fischer) and is not itself a court or board record. It describes cost overruns, not a skim of construction funds by Siegel.
